name: Fadogia agrestis
description: Stem of a West African shrub (also classified as Vangueria agrestis) used in traditional medicine

status.usStatus: Dietary supplement · not an approved drug

note.text: Research is in rats, mostly from one group in Nigeria. 5 of 17 supplements tested had none of the plant’s marker compounds.

bullets: **In rats,** blood testosterone and mating measures rose over 5 days
**In rats,** 28 days changed testicular, liver and kidney measures
**In people,** the mechanism is not established
No human studies or registered trials found
Rat toxicity signs in testes, liver, kidney

practical.routes: Not studied in people (by mouth in rats)
practical.soldAs: Dietary supplement; not FDA reviewed before sale
practical.monitored: No human trials; rat studies measured testosterone, organs

regulatory.text: No approved drug; sold as dietary supplement

references: Asian J Androl, Fadogia agrestis and sexual behavior in male rats, Dec 2005
J Ethnopharmacol, Fadogia agrestis and testicular function in rats, Jan 2008
Planta Med, analysis of Fadogia agrestis supplements, Jan 2019
